subject: Baseline parking & warmup GPU fleet options for Astera Health
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@asterahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Baseline parking & warmup GPU fleet options for Astera Health

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is a short options memo describing three dedicated-capacity approaches that line up with the usage profile you shared (spikey nightly batch inference + steady daytime interactive traffic). High level: we focused on predictable latency for peak windows while keeping committed spend reasonable.

Summary of the three approaches (see attached pdf for cost pro formas):

1) Baseline-parking (lower commit, pre-warm on schedule)
   - Minimum parked baseline: 40 reserved GPUs (kept idle but billed)
   - Pre-warm window: automatic warm-up of an additional 60 GPUs 45 minutes before nightly batch start; warm nodes come out of parked pool to avoid cold-start latency
   - Best for teams that want predictable peak latency without a large up-front commit

2) Progressive-onramp (staged commit)
   - Initial commit 80 GPUs; commit increases on a 3-month cadence to 160 GPUs based on usage triggers
   - Autoscaling above commit for burst (pay-as-you-go)
   - Good fit if you expect steady growth and want to step commitments with product milestones

3) Pre-warm + burst-lane (higher baseline, lower cold starts)
   - Baseline 120 reserved GPUs with a 20% burst buffer for sustained spikes
   - Overnight maintenance/pre-warm nodes pinned for faster KV cache priming
   - Best where SLA/99p latency for batch and interactive traffic is critical

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on your persistent lanes; pre-warmed nodes will reduce median token latency by ~30-45ms in our benchmarks.
- Billing model: committed monthly reservations + metered burst. Parking credits can be applied to reduce effective cost during off-peak months.
- We included a suggested warm-up cron (45/30/15 minutes pre-window) and an activation safety net (graceful fallback to hosted lower-cost models if burst exceeds capacity).

Attachment: Astera-Capacity-Options-20260331.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

If you like, I can sketch a mutual action plan (MAP) with ramp milestones and procurement checkpoints. What looks closest to your internal procurement comfort zone?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Markus — quick internal note before we hear back from Sophie.

A few considerations I want documented so we give a clean recommendation:
- Min GPUs for idle baseline: confirm they understand billed-but-parked behavior (network egress still billed if they use pre-warmed nodes to serve external traffic).
- Warm-up timing: 45 minutes should be safe for models with ~16k KV priming; call this out as conservative. We can drop to 30m for smaller models.
- SLA ask: if they want a 99th percentile SL latency guarantee during nightly batch, that leans us toward option 3 or a hybrid (baseline 80 + guaranteed pre-warm pool of 40).
- Contract/commit cadence: if procurement needs quarterly reviews, offer a 3-month staircase with an exit window after month 6 with pro-rated credits.

Ben — want me to include a short cost delta table for the three approaches? I can add estimated $/token and monthly effective committed spend.

Priya

Hi Markus / Priya —

Thanks for this — the memo is useful and aligns with a few internal ideas. A couple quick answers and asks from our side:

1) We prefer a hybrid approach: start with Baseline-parking at 60 reserved GPUs + a pinned pre-warm pool of 40 GPUs that spin up 45 minutes before our nightly batch window. That should manage our cold-start sensitivity.

2) Procurement timeline: we need an 8-week lead time for contract and security review. Can you provide a MAP and a procurement-ready SOW that lists activation dates, SLAs, and data controls?

3) Can you call out a fallback strategy if bursts exceed the reserved + burst-lane? We need to know whether traffic will gracefully spill to hosted instances or if requests will queue/fail.

4) Pricing ask: is there a one-off onboarding credit or parking-credit to offset the first-month parked baseline? We have a month-one usage cliff we want to smooth.

If you can send a short MAP and a concise SOW we can circulate to legal and procurement.

Best,
Sophie
VP, ML Infrastructure
Astera Health

Sophie — thanks for the clarity. Confirming next steps and commitments below so procurement has something concise to review.

Proposed near-term MAP (attached spreadsheet):
- Week 0 (sign): Activate Baseline-parking 60 reserved GPUs. Apply one-month onboarding parking credit equal to 25% of the baseline monthly commitment.
- Week 2: Enable pinned pre-warm pool of 40 GPUs; configure warm-up cron at 45 minutes prior to nightly batch window.
- Week 6: Observability check-in (latency heatmap, token economics, KV cache hit-rate); option to transition to staircase ramp if usage warrant (documented triggers in the MAP).
- Procurement: we will deliver a procurement-ready SOW that lists activation dates, data controls (VPC peering option, KMS integration), and SLA language for availability and 99p tail latency for pre-warmed lanes.

Fallback behavior: by default, Redwood will route excess burst to a pay-as-you-go hosted lane compatible with the model (same model family, quantization profile). Requests will not be dropped; they will be routed to the hosted lane with a latency delta note in the response headers. We will add an explicit canary policy in the SOW so you control whether to allow spillover or enforce strict capacity gating.

Attachments: Astera-MAP-20260407.xlsx (xlsx, 85KB), Astera-Capacity-Options-20260331.pdf

Ben / Priya — please take ownership of the SOW and MAP edits; I'll prepare the procurement email template and deliverables. Sophie, I'll loop in Solutions Engineering for an onboarding readiness call next week.

Thanks,
Markus
